market_context: A relief rally is under way after last week's AI-led rout, when the Nasdaq fell about 10% in its worst week since 2020. Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO after Trump urged the board to do so, and NVDA is up about 35%. The S&P 500 is up about 4.6% and the Nasdaq about 6.8%, but the VIX is still near 28.6 and the 10-year yield is 4.95%. PCE inflation is due Wednesday, and some strategists are calling this a 'dead cat bounce'.

predictions.reasoning: NVDA is trading at the very top of its day range ($169.29 high) after a roughly 35% one-day gap on a single news catalyst. Gaps this large often partly fade as early buyers take profits. Probes into the foreign-intelligence matter are still ongoing, and the stock is still down about 39% over the past month.
TSLA is up 12% on a sympathy rally, trading near its $389.59 high. With the VIX still near 28 and the 10-year yield at 4.95%, the index is vulnerable to profit-taking into the holiday-shortened week.

SPY is up 4.6% on a largely mechanical rebound, trading near the high of its range, and the S&P is still more than 10% off its October 6 high. Capital Economics calls the move a 'dead cat bounce', and PCE inflation on Wednesday plus thin holiday trading make some intraday giveback likely.
